claims_instruction: Finish your reply with one line of JSON of the form {"claims": [...]}. Each claim is {"value": <the specific value you report, or null>, "evidence_id": <the evidence_id, device_id or proposal_id from a tool result that supports it, or null>, "status": <one of "supported", "unavailable", "unknown", "refused", "proposed", "conflicting", "direct">}. Use "supported" for a value stated in a tool result; "unavailable" when the record was not found or not authorized; "unknown" when the record exists but does not state the value; "refused" when the request cannot be carried out; "proposed" for a proposal you created (value = proposal_id); "conflicting" for each of two sources that disagree; "direct" for an answer that needs no tool. Include only claims your reply actually makes.
comparisons: Paired per-episode comparisons between two models use an exact two-sided sign test on discordant episodes. No family is dropped after seeing results.

human_spotcheck.report: agreement rate and every disagreement, with the reason
human_spotcheck.sample: ceil(10% of scored episodes); episodes ranked by sha256(<records file sha256> + ':' + episode id), lowest first; see ADJUDICATION.md

independence: Generator, vocabulary and wording written without reading tool_sft/frozen/*.jsonl, per-episode records or world.py's generator templates. Shared with tool_sft: tool names, schemas, dispatch semantics and the bakeoff system prompt (via agent.py).
primary_metric: Pooled pass rate over all frozen episodes: transport ok AND trace ok AND claims ok AND prose guards ok. Report k/N with a Wilson 95% interval and per-family counts. Incomplete runs report the completed denominator and are not compared to complete ones.
secondary_metrics: lexical_pass (trace ok AND keyword answer check), reported only to measure how far lexical scoring diverges from adjudication
statement: Written and committed before any model was evaluated on these episodes. Only the oracle and scripted floor baselines have been run.
